- **Green stems** that remain bright/fresh green
- **Dried, tan/brown pods** that appear shriveled and flat/empty
- Stems are green while pods have dried — a hallmark contrast
- Plant is near soil level with dried debris around it

This strongly suggests **Green_stem_disorder** — stems stay green while pods and foliage dry prematurely. Let me verify with reference images.
The Green_stem_disorder reference is an **excellent match** — green stems with dried tan pods, same setting near soil. Let me check a couple more candidates to be thorough.
Sudden_death_syndrome and Diaporthe don't match — they show leaf mottling and stem rot lesions respectively. Let me view two more to meet the minimum.

Charcoal_Rot and Brown_Stem_Rot both show stem discoloration and root/internal rot — clearly different from the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**

| Feature | Test Image | Green_stem_disorder |
|---|---|---|
| Stem color | Bright green | Bright green ✓ |
| Pod appearance | Dried, tan, flat/empty | Dried, tan, flat ✓ |
| Setting | Near soil, dried debris | Same ✓ |
| Contrast | Green stems vs dried pods | Defining hallmark ✓ |

The test image is an unmistakable case of Green_stem_disorder — the stems remain photosynthetically active and green while pods have dried and matured. The reference collage contains nearly identical images.
